questions.prompt: A budget is…
questions.explanation: A budget is a plan that tells your money where to go.

questions.prompt: Making a plan BEFORE you spend helps you not run out of money.
questions.explanation: True! That's exactly what a budget does.

questions.prompt: You have ${a}. You plan to spend ${b}. How much is left to save?
questions.explanation: ${a} − ${b} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Which three jars make a good money plan?
questions.explanation: Save for later, spend on things you need and want, and share to help others.

questions.prompt: You get ${a} a week. You save ${s} each week. How much do you save in 4 weeks?
questions.explanation: ${s} × 4 = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Your budget says $5 for snacks this week. You've spent $5 by Wednesday. What's smart?
choices: Wait until next week for more snacks
Take money from your savings jar
Borrow from a friend every day
questions.explanation: Sticking to your plan helps your savings grow.

questions.prompt: You earned ${e}. You want to save 1/4 of it. How much do you save?
questions.explanation: ${e} ÷ 4 = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Why should a budget have a little extra for surprises?
choices: Because unexpected things happen, like a broken bike
So you can buy more candy
questions.explanation: Surprises happen! A little extra keeps your plan safe.

questions.prompt: Your monthly budget: $40 total. Needs $20, Save $10, Share $4. How much can you spend on fun?
Two of the same juice boxes: one costs $1, one costs $2. Which is the better deal?
questions.explanation: Same juice, lower price = better deal!

questions.prompt: A $10 toy is half off. What does it cost now?
questions.explanation: Half of $10 is $5.

questions.prompt: A store has a sale on something you don't need. Is it a good deal for YOU?
choices: No, spending money on something you don't need isn't saving
questions.explanation: A sale only saves money if you were going to buy it anyway.

questions.prompt: A ${p} shirt is ${d} off. What do you pay?
questions.explanation: ${p} − ${d} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A $20 game is 10% off. How much do you save?
A pack of 10 pencils costs $2. A pack of 4 costs $1. Which costs less per pencil?
questions.explanation: 10 for $2 is 20¢ each. 4 for $1 is 25¢ each.

questions.prompt: Apples are ${p} each. You buy {n}. How much?
questions.explanation: ${p} × {n} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A $40 jacket is 25% off. What is the sale price?
'Buy one, get one free' is a good deal when…
questions.explanation: Two for the price of one only saves money if you'll use both.

questions.prompt: You pay $5 for a $4 sandwich. How much change?
You buy gum for {c}¢ and pay with $1. How many cents of change?
questions.explanation: 100¢ − {c}¢ = {ANSWER:int}¢.

questions.prompt: Which coins make 30 cents?
Price ${p}. You pay with $10. Change?
questions.explanation: Count up from ${p} to $10: ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: What's the fewest coins to make 40 cents?
questions.explanation: 25 + 10 + 5 = 40 with just 3 coins.

questions.prompt: Your groceries cost ${p}. You pay with $20. Change?
London uses pounds (£). The USA uses dollars ($). To shop in London with dollars you need to…
questions.explanation: Different countries use different money. You exchange one for another.

questions.prompt: If $1 gets you 2 Fin-coins, how many Fin-coins for $7?
Exchange booths make money by…
choices: Charging fees or giving a slightly worse rate
questions.explanation: Booths earn money with fees or rates that favor them.

questions.prompt: $1 = £0.80. How many pounds for $10?
Paying money each month to live in a home someone else owns is called…
questions.explanation: Renters pay rent to the owner (landlord) each month.

questions.prompt: If you OWN your home and the roof leaks, who pays to fix it?
questions.explanation: Owners pay for repairs. Renters usually call the landlord.

questions.prompt: A family will move to a new city in one year. Should they rent or buy?
choices: Rent, buying and selling a home costs a lot for a short stay
questions.explanation: For short stays, renting is usually cheaper and easier.

questions.prompt: The big loan people use to buy a home is called a…
questions.explanation: A mortgage is a loan for a home, paid back over many years.

questions.prompt: Groceries for dinner are a…
questions.explanation: Food is a need.

questions.prompt: Which is a want on a shopping trip?
questions.explanation: The toy car is fun but not needed.

questions.prompt: Store brand cereal is $2. A famous brand of the same size is $4. They taste almost the same. Smart choice?
questions.explanation: Store brands are often just as good and cost less.

questions.prompt: Before you go shopping, it helps to…
questions.explanation: A list helps you buy what you need and skip impulse buys.

questions.prompt: Milk: 1 bottle for $3, or 2 bottles for $5. How much do you save buying 2 for $5 instead of 2 single bottles?
questions.explanation: 2 × $3 = $6. $6 − $5 = $1 saved, if you'll drink it all!

questions.prompt: Writing down what you spend helps you…
questions.explanation: Tracking spending shows you where your money really goes.

questions.prompt: If you spend more than you planned, your budget needs fixing, not ignoring.
questions.explanation: True! Adjust your plan or your spending.

questions.prompt: A bus pass is $10 a week. Where should it go in your budget?
questions.explanation: Getting to school is a need.

questions.prompt: Your Share jar money could…
questions.explanation: Share money helps others!

questions.prompt: Weekly allowance $12. You save half and share $2. How much is left to spend?
Prices at the airport are often higher. Why?
choices: Travelers have fewer other choices there
questions.explanation: When buyers have few choices, sellers can charge more.

questions.prompt: You have 3 quarters and 2 dimes. How many cents?
In winter, umbrellas and coats sell a lot. In summer, what sells a lot?
questions.explanation: What people want changes with the seasons. That's demand!

questions.prompt: You want a $30 skateboard and can save $5 a week. Your budget plan should…
choices: Buy it today with money you don't have
Spend the $5 on candy each week
questions.explanation: $5 × 6 weeks = $30. A plan gets you there!

questions.prompt: A price tag says $3. You have $2. Can you buy it?
questions.explanation: $2 is less than $3, so you need $1 more.

questions.prompt: Rent is $500 a month. How much rent in 3 months?
An ad says 'Only 2 left! Buy NOW!' This is meant to make you…
questions.explanation: Rushing you is a trick to stop you from comparing. Take your time!

questions.prompt: Three friends split a $13.50 bill evenly. How much does each pay?
A good budget only has needs and no fun at all.
questions.explanation: False! Planning some fun is part of a happy budget.

questions.prompt: A coupon gives $2 off a $9 book. What do you pay?
